passage: I'm Rukmini, a designer at the agency. Kamal joined in June as an "intern". He works nine to eight, handles client files on his own, and gets no stipend. When he asked what he would learn, he was told "we'll see about a job later". Last Friday I saw him at the pantry with a small notebook, muttering. He had written two questions for the manager: what stipend, and what learning goals. The manager said, "We'll see." Kamal nodded, smiled tightly and wrote a date at the end of the month in his notebook. I can't tell if he is afraid, angry or just resolved. On Monday I saw him updating his CV in the lunch break, with the agency line still on it.

qa.q: Which month did Kamal join the agency?
What might Kamal be feeling about losing the agency line on his CV?
qa.a: Kamal may be afraid of losing it while also feeling used, though Rukmini admits she can't tell if he is afraid, angry or resolved.

qa.q: What should Kamal do if nothing changes by the date in his notebook?
qa.a: Kamal should walk away as planned and keep the updated CV and other applications moving, since he has asked his questions and set a limit.

qa.q: How does Rukmini seem to see Kamal's situation?
qa.a: Rukmini seems sympathetic and watchful; she notices the long hours, the missing stipend and the vague answers, but is careful not to claim she knows what Kamal feels.

grounding: An unpaid full-time intern feels used but fears losing the CV line, asks about stipend and learning goals and sets a time limit.

passage: Monday, 11 p.m. Divyansh's diary. Week seven of the 'internship' at the marketing agency. Today I made 42 cold calls, formatted Kashish-ma'am's slides and fetched lunch for the whole team. I've learned nothing new since week two. No stipend, and every time I ask about the 'full-time role after', the answer is 'let's see'. I feel used, and I also feel scared, because this is the only line on my CV that isn't college. So here's the plan, written down so I can't back out. Tomorrow I ask Kashish-ma'am for fifteen minutes. Three questions: is there any stipend, what exactly will I learn in the next month, and when will the full-time decision be made. I'll give it until the end of next month. If nothing changes by then, I leave and keep the seven weeks on my CV anyway. That line is already mine.

qa.q: How many cold calls did Divyansh make today?
What two feelings pull at Divyansh?
qa.a: Divyansh feels used, and also scared of losing the only non-college line on the CV.

qa.q: Why is Divyansh's plan a good one?
qa.a: Asking about a stipend, learning and a decision date, then setting a deadline to leave, stops the unpaid work from running on forever.

qa.q: How might Kashish-ma'am see Divyansh's request for fifteen minutes?
qa.a: Kashish-ma'am may be surprised, but it gives a clear chance to explain what the internship offers or to admit it offers little.

grounding: A diary shows an unpaid internship that is really full-time work, and a plan to ask about stipend and learning goals, set a time limit and walk if nothing changes.
